note: Both sets capture the core optical facts correctly (M1→M2→M3 light path, protected-aluminum coating under UV operation, instrument field-of-view positions, ray collimation toward a common on-axis pupil plane). Set A pads its list with many near-duplicate claims (UVS/starshade/coronagraph position vs. location, instrument deployment vs. location, combined ray claim duplicating two others) plus a trivial components-label claim. Set B is cleaner and adds a substantive tradeoff claim A omits: rear mounting may increase overall telescope spacecraft height. Neither set extracts the Table 5.5-1 numeric parameters (diameters, radii of curvature, thicknesses, spacings, M3 coating 'Varies').
remarks: Both sets miss all of Table 5.5-1 (M1/M2/M3 diameter 4,000/450/680 mm, radius of curvature 19,800/-1,953/-2,168 mm, thickness 420/100/100 mm, spacing to next optic 9,030/9,080 mm, M3 coating 'Varies') — the most quantitatively valuable content on the page. The 'M2 | directed relationship | M3' claim in both sets is loosely bound (the quoted sentence's subject is M1), though the light path M2→M3 is supported; it does not differentiate the sets. Set A's position/location pairs for UVS, starshade and coronagraph are the same fact stated twice under two attribute names.
